title: New directions in dynamical expectation estimation
authors: Panjin Kim, Kyung Chul Jeong, Yun-Tak Oh
abstract: Computing dynamical expectation values typically relies on approximations optimized for the state or observable separately, without accounting for how their errors combine in the final expression.This work explores an alternative approach in which each approximation is guided by both the state and the observable, accounting for how they jointly determine the target expectation value. This idea is implemented through a sweep algorithm with coupled loss functions for forward state and backward observable updates. Exact error relations provide an analytical rationale for how the proposed losses can improve the accuracy. Numerical tests on 30-qubit random circuits show errors two to three orders of magnitude smaller than those of variational state compression at equal bond dimensions. These results motivate further exploration of joint state and observable approximation for dynamical expectation value estimation.
summary: This paper proposes a novel 'sweep algorithm' to accurately estimate dynamical expectation values in quantum circuits by jointly optimizing approximations for both the quantum state and the observable. By deriving an analytical error decomposition, the method shows significant error reduction compared to existing techniques, making it a powerful tool for simulating quantum dynamics.
main_problem: Dynamically estimating expectation values in quantum systems is challenging because conventional approximation methods optimize the state or observable separately, failing to account for the combined error in the final expectation value.
main_result: The proposed joint state and observable approximation algorithm achieves errors two to three orders of magnitude smaller than variational state compression on 30-qubit random circuits.
method: The authors introduce a 'sweep algorithm' utilizing coupled loss functions that jointly guide the approximation of the quantum state and the observable, derived from an analytical error decomposition.

paper_structure: The paper first identifies the error combination problem, develops the joint loss-guided sweep algorithm, provides an analytical error decomposition ($E^{-b}(i) = R(i)_1 + R(i)_2$), and validates the method using numerical tests on large random circuits.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, numerically superior framework for calculating time-dependent expectation values, which is crucial for simulating quantum dynamics in complex systems where simple state or observable approximations fail.
